runs.final_answer:
**Supported fact**

Apple’s current security-releases index says the latest version of macOS is **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2**, and in the security-updates table it lists **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2** as a macOS security release with release date **August 17, 2026**. (https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100)

Apple’s security-content page for that update identifies the affected system as **macOS Tahoe** and says **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2** was **released August 17, 2026**. (https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)

Apple’s security-content page for **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2** lists multiple fixed issues, including **Audio**, **ImageIO**, **IOGPUFamily**, **Kernel**, **WebKit**, **WebKit History**, and **WebKit Storage** vulnerabilities. (https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)

**Inference from Apple’s page**

I do **not** see Apple mark any **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2** issue as actively exploited on that page. This is an **inference from absence**: Apple’s page lists the CVEs and impacts, but the page does not include Apple’s usual exploitation language such as “Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been actively exploited” or “...exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack...” anywhere in the listed entries I reviewed. (https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)

So, based on Apple’s own published security-content page, the most recent macOS security update is **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2**, it affects **macOS Tahoe systems**, and **Apple does not identify any actively exploited issues in that update**. The last clause is still an **inference from the page’s omission**, not an explicit Apple sentence saying “none.” (https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100, https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)

**Uncertainty / lack of good evidence**

There is no good evidence on the **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2** page that Apple intended this update for **macOS Sequoia** or **macOS Sonoma**; Apple’s releases index separately lists newer Sequoia and Sonoma security updates only up to **August 6, 2026**, not August 17, 2026. (https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100)

I found no disagreement within the Apple pages I checked, but Apple’s wording does not explicitly state “this update contains no actively exploited vulnerabilities,” so that specific conclusion remains an **absence-based inference** rather than a direct quotation. (https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)
